text.name: rf_pda_side_info_dairy
text.text: This pause page is your barn herd glance. Each row is one dairy barn: herd score, the milk sale quality you would get today, and spoilage stage. Honesty: the live spoilage clock does not start until a collection is recorded, and that path is currently inert (no collection writer wired). Fresh often means the clock never started, not that milk is actively ageing on a timer. Sale quality still shows the effective tier the barn data carries. Warnings for feed disease or mycotoxin appear only when the barn data already carries them. Esc does not schedule collections, change contracts, or set feed fields. Quiet when Precision Farming is active.

text.text: Two clocks: Herd now counts the milking animals standing in the barn today. Milk in tank follows the stored milk by the breeds that produced it, so a new herd beside old milk is normal. Unknown milk predates the record or arrived unproven.

text.name: dairy_rf_pda_side_teach
text.text:
Dairy
One card per barn on your farm. Turn pages with , and . or the pager.
Herd now is the milking herd in the barn today, by breed. Milk in tank is the stored milk by the breeds that made it. Milk with no breed record stays unknown. A new herd beside old milk is normal.
Spoilage clock: starts when a collection is recorded. Clock idle means not started, so Fresh is not a live timer yet.
Feed disease clock: diseased feed in the pool puts mycotoxin on the herd. It fades day by day. The page hint names the barn while it lasts.
Stored feed: quality is locked on the crop at the cut and blended in the farm's silos. The trough draws from that pool and milk follows it. Organic means over 80% organic share. Waiting for harvest data until the first cut is recorded.
